audit_findings.title: Acquisition earn-out liabilities are omitted from the common-equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.200m filed liability at 2026-03-31, equal to $0.251 per diluted share and 7.2% of base equity value; filed maximum exposure is $41.000m
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds $39.688m of cash but does not subtract contingent acquisition consideration, a senior claim not captured by equity-level owner earnings retaining interest expense.
audit_findings.evidence: Changes in assumptions and operating results could have a significant impact on the earn-out amount up to a maximum of $ 45,501 , through earn-out periods measured through March 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission. The liability and cash coexist on the same March 2026 balance sheet, and the expected $12.2m payment is large relative to the $170m base equity value. The maximum is not the expected deduction, but it shows additional estimation risk.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $12.200m contingent-consideration balance and any fixed post-closing acquisition payables, determine whether any projected owner earnings already fund them, and rerun every scenario and buy-below price with unpaid consideration deducted exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ignores a post-anchor acquisition and its 20% outside ownership
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed redeemable noncontrolling interest of $1.210m, or $0.025 per diluted share; total Weport earnings and perimeter effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 owner-earnings anchor predates Weport, while the March 2026 cash, debt and other bridge balances follow the acquisition. Excluding Weport earnings can understate value, while omitting the outside owners' 20% claim and future purchase obligation can overstate it.
audit_findings.evidence: Effective September 1, 2025 , the Company acquired an 80 % stock ownership interest in Weport, S.A. de C.V. (“Weport”), a Mexico City-based, privately held company.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not isolate Weport's owner earnings or the ultimate redemption price. The known $1.210m noncontrolling claim is only 0.7% of base equity value, but that amount does not measure the omitted earnings or future 20% purchase obligation, so total materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Build a Weport-only reconciliation covering acquisition consideration, financing, post-acquisition owner earnings, the 80% attributable share, the $1.210m redeemable interest and the put/call redemption formula; then rerun on one consistent pre- or post-acquisition perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may treat serial acquisitions as free reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed acquisition cash spending of $28.534m in FY2025 and $6.812m in FY2024; respectively 306.8% and 73.2% of the $9.3m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The scenarios compound owner earnings at 3% to 6% without an explicit acquisition-reinvestment charge, although acquired businesses contribute earnings obtained through purchase consideration and earn-outs outside ordinary capital expenditure.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash paid for acquisitions were $28.5 million and $6.8 million for the fiscal years ended June 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The large historical acquisition spending is demonstrated; it is not demonstrated that the scenario growth rates depend on continued acquisitions. Nevertheless, the spending scale is more than three times anchor owner earnings in FY2025, so treating acquisition-supported growth as costless is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Separate organic from acquired changes in owner earnings for each historical year and rerun the scenarios either with organic growth alone or with normalized acquisition cash consideration, fixed payments and earn-outs charged as reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated VIE cash flows can exceed the common shareholders' economic claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Known outside-owner income was $0.147m in FY2025, 1.6% of the $9.3m anchor, and $0.512m in FY2024; the cash-flow mismatch is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An owner-earnings calculation can mix net income attributable to RLGT with consolidated depreciation, working-capital and capital-spending amounts that include 60% of RLP economics belonging to RCP.
audit_findings.evidence: RCP’s ownership interest entitles it to 60 % of the profits and distributable cash, if any, generated by RLP.
audit_findings.explanation: The 60% outside economic interest and consolidation are demonstrated. The supplied figures quantify only the reported noncontrolling-income allocation, which is small relative to the latest anchor, not the outside share of every cash-flow adjustment or the cited historical gaps. The record therefore cannot establish the full valuation magnitude.
audit_findings.action: For every historical year, reconcile owner earnings from net income attributable to RLGT through each consolidated cash-flow adjustment and remove RCP's share of RLP depreciation, working capital, reinvestment and other cash flows; rerun the trend if differences are found.

audit_findings.title: A contingent-consideration remeasurement gain could inflate the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed FY2025 gain of $2.491m, equal to 26.8% of the $9.3m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If the noncash gain remains in the earnings starting point without a reversing adjustment, it increases anchor owner earnings and all forecast and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: Change in fair value of contingent consideration was a gain of $2.5 million for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, compared to a gain of $0.5 million for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention of the gain is not demonstrated because the owner-earnings reconciliation was not supplied; the filed cash-flow statement itself reverses the $2.491m gain when reconciling operating cash flow. If the valuation independently retained it, however, the potential error is more than one-quarter of the anchor and is material.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $2.491m gain through the FY2025 owner-earnings worksheet. If it was retained, remove it exactly once and rerun the anchor, all scenario present values and the buy-below price; if already reversed through operating cash flow, document that linkage.

audit_findings.title: A material lease-exit charge may depress the latest-year anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed FY2025 charge of $1.491m, equal to 16.0% of the $9.3m anchor; an additional $0.165m was filed for the first nine months of FY2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining a genuinely exceptional charge reduces anchor owner earnings and forecast value; adding it back when lease exits are recurring integration or expansion costs would instead overstate owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended June 30, 2025, the Company recorded lease termination costs of $ 1,491 for exiting an existing warehouse facility prior to the conclusion of the lease term and relocating to a larger facility in British Columbia to expand its existing operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge and its potentially material scale are demonstrated, but its treatment in the anchor is not. The additional FY2026 lease-termination costs show that the category did not disappear entirely, so a full add-back cannot be presumed without a normalization analysis.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $1.491m charge through the FY2025 owner-earnings reconciliation, compile multi-year lease-exit and relocation costs including the FY2026 $0.165m, determine a normalized recurring amount, and rerun all scenarios using only the supported exceptional portion as an adjustment.
